newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- The Western Cape provincial government has defied Finance Minister Trevor Manuel by opting to budget for a deficit of 247 million rand for the 1997/98 fiscal year.

- Members of national and provincial public accounts committees are planning proposals to increase their powers, which they regard as "totally inadequate" for ensuring financial discipline in government.
- Annual private sector credit growth remained high in February, ticking up to 17.34 percent from January's revised 17.06 percent, according to Reserve Bank figures.
- Telkom sustained direct losses of almost 40 million rand and indirect losses of 190 million rand in the 11 months to February as a result of copper cable theft, managing director Brian Clark said.
- Retail group LA Retail Stores Ltd has acquired branded apparel and footwear marketer and distributor Skye Products for 115.6 million rand, effectively trebling the group's size.
- The government plans to oppose a bid in the Cape Town High Court by about 50 Western Cape schools to overturn provisions governing the employment of teachers by public schools.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Fears that the withdrawal of senior British officials would lead to the collapse of key customs projects were played down by Piet Liebenberg, head of the South African Revenue Service.
- Khehla Mthembu, the chairman of New Age Beverages, said his company was not in serious trouble resulting from the poor structuring of a deal with Pepsico to bottle Pepsi products in South Africa.

- LA Retail Stores, which listed on the JSE less than six months ago, has trebled in size with the 115.6 million rand acquisition of Skye Products, the country's largest distributor of branded apparel and footwear.

- Hopes for an interest rate cut before the third quarter were dealt a severe blow Reserve Bank data showing growth in private sector credit extension had edged higher in February for the second month in a row.

- The amounts of money being bandied about for the Maputo Corridor linking Gauteng and Mozambique's major port keep growing abd projects relating to the planned corridor could amount to as much as 23 billion rand.
THE STAR
- Weeks of rain in greater Johannesburg have taken a heavy toll, with homeless shelters full and road repairs falling behind as dangerous potholes appear throughout the network.
- A detective academy to provide advanced and specialised training for police investigators is to be established to improve crime fighting capabilities of the police force.
- Johannesburg's Eastern council budget was approved by its executive committee without members seeing a detailed breakdown of income and expenditure, lawyers said.
- Western Cape police have accepted independent findings that police who initially investigated a rape case on Robben Island were insensitive and negligent.
